newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on feed ideas, soybean rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on feed ideas, soybean rally.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended higher on Tuesday, boosted by ideas U.S. feed usage would increase as pork producers raced to meet demand left by Taiwan's pork export ban, traders said.
"The instant improvement in the hog feeding margins (due to Taiwan's export ban) has created a lot of pricing," said E.D. and F. Man International analyst Charlie Sernatinger.

A Taiwanese agriculture official said the outbreak of foot and mouth disease could keep Taiwanese pork exports out of the Japanese market for as many as five years. Japan is the largest buyer of Taiwanese pork.
Taiwanese buyers have said the export ban could cut Taiwan's 1997 feed corn imports by 20 percent.
Singapore on Tuesday added its name to the list of countries refusing to import Taiwanese pork.
Floor sources also pointed to news some cash basis bids rose early Tuesday on increased demand for corn in the southeast United States, a major pork producing region.
Traders said activity was subdued ahead of Monday's USDA prospective plantings and quarterly stocks report.
Corn ended 4-1/4 to two cents per bushel higher with May up 3-1/4 at $3.02-1/4.

Corn exports remained quiet as world buyers opted for lower priced Argentine corn. Exporters said U.S. corn was priced at $129 per ton, FOB U.S. Gulf for April shipment. Argentine corn cost $117.60 per ton for April shipment.
Thai feed mills were seeking up to 200,000 tonnes of corn but sources there said they would likely buy from Argentina.
"We will also look at the United States and South Africa. The current prices are a bit expensive but I guess we need to order soon," a feed producer told Reuters.

Corn closed above the four- and 20-day moving averages and short term technical indicators remained bullish, technicians said. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the May closed at 53 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought at least 2.5 million bushels December and two million July while ADM bought one million December and 1.5 million July, traders said.
ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp bought three million December and one million March 1998 while LFG, LIT America and E.D. and F. Man International each sold one million May.
In options, ABN-AMRO bought 1,600 December $3.20 calls at 15-1/2 to 15-3/4 cents.
ABN-AMRO also bought 850 December $2.80 puts and 850 December $3.00 calls at five cents.
Lind-Waldock sold 1,000 December $2.80 puts at 20-1/2 to 20-3/4 cents and Rosenthal Collins sold 600 December $3.20 calls at 15-1/4.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 55,366 contracts.
